pinned_upstream.content_access: git show <commit>:<path>; checkout and build tree were not read or changed

current_review_scope: Dependency licence inputs are unchanged from the existing review; the qualified R4 native profile includes changed first-party allocator/runtime code. Final candidate consumer output comparison and final binary/licence review remain required; no publication authorization.

evidence_limits: Historical generator execution logs and five historical M0 generated-header copies are unavailable. The delivered current generated files are associated with exact current compile commands/objects; this is documented and does not assert byte-reproducible historical C compilation.
Publisher CI must authenticate the final candidate and all material digests before R1-A6 can close. This review does not replace protected provenance or independent final acceptance.
findings: AROS pinned root LICENSE section 5.2 applies APL 1.1 subject to preserved LEGAL/file-level exceptions. The linked 23 archive members and startup source are mapped; stdc BSD memmove/strlcpy/strlcat exceptions do not occur in this link map. No mapped path falls under the root GPL exceptions.

AROS-derived Rust declarations retain APL scope in the crate license and dated modifications. Additional original contributions retain the owner-selected MIT OR Apache-2.0 grant without relicensing Covered Code.

341 exact or explicitly comment-adjusted corresponding source/notices files are delivered in the same-media capsule, including 24 C compilation dependency closures, generator/configuration/build-rule inputs, Boost headers and original BSL text; full archive readback passes.

Generated-source private prefixes are changed only in automatically generated comments, with before/after SHA records and unchanged non-comment bytes. The startup symbol rename and ABI translations are recorded with dates and original AROS origin.

Full locked Rust crate/runtime notices are preserved. Cargo patch notices are checked against pinned Git; openssl-src notices are checked against the complete registry archive checksum from pinned Cargo.lock, not only mutable checksum JSON.

External qualified toolchain/C SDK/vendor prerequisites are inventoried and separately provisioned; they are not redistributed as bundled prerequisites. This review does not assign a single license to entire mixed C SDK archives.
decision.first_party_owner_decision: MIT OR Apache-2.0, explicitly selected by Fabian Schmieder
decision.scope: Exact source SDK and retained R3 native SHAUTIL, with same-media corresponding sources/notices; no publication authorization
